title: HHS-04-R1: GAO-24-106276 Recommendation 1 artifact scope audit
publisher: U.S. Government Accountability Office and named implementing agency
summary: GAO-24-106276 Recommendation 1 remains Open – Partially Addressed. Phase 56S checks three directive elements and classifies the public document result as no separately public response artifact located.
key_findings: Availability class: No separately public response artifact located.
Repository finding: The official repository pass did not locate a separate public copy of the exact response artifact as of the capture date; this does not prove the artifact does not exist.
Scope element 1: Department-wide coordination procedures — Not established by located public record. No separately public SOP located.
Scope element 2: Use across HHS component agencies — Not established by located public record. No public exercise or response record demonstrates operation.
Scope element 3: After-action report documenting coordination — Not established by located public record. No qualifying public AAR located.
FTFN public-scope check: 0 supported, 0 partial, and 3 not established across three directive elements.
GAO acceptance state: GAO classifies Recommendation 1 Open – Partially Addressed.

Continuation rule: Continue the Phase 56R rule and recheck exact agency repositories plus the GAO product page when a named artifact or status changes. An availability result or FTFN scope check cannot substitute for GAO acceptance.
why_it_matters: Document-level scope checks show exactly what a public artifact covers, what remains unavailable, and why availability cannot be converted into implementation or closure.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves HHS-04 and its exact recommendation identity.
Records an official repository search trail and explicit public-availability result.
Separates FTFN's visible-scope check from GAO acceptance, implementation, closure, and operating outcomes.
evidence_limits: Not publicly located does not mean nonexistent or withheld.
A public document may be scope-adjacent without being the exact implementation artifact.
FTFN document-scope findings do not substitute for GAO's recommendation-status decision.
Document evidence does not establish performance, readiness, safety, savings, value, ranking, composite score, or causation.
